info.bio:
Suicide es un dúo synthpunk de los años '70 y '80, conformado por Alan Vega (vocalista) y Martin Rev (sintetizador y batería electrónica). Fue formado a principios de los 70s como un grupo convencional de rock, con guitarras, bajos y batería, pero poco a poco los miembros del grupo desertaron, hasta que solo quedaron Vega y Rev.

Los riffs de teclado de Rev—usualmente provenientes de un desgastado órgano y acompañados de una primitiva batería electrónica—eran simples e hipnóticos, y proveían un fondo ideal para la voz de Vega. Vega le debía gran parte de estilo a Elvis Presley y cantantes de rockabilly, pero su canto de alaridos y murmullos nerviosos era único.

Suicide emergió de la temprana escena punk de Nueva York con una reputación de presentaciones feroces y controversiales, que ocasionalmente llevaban a distubios y violencia.

Su primer álbum, el epónimo Suicide, es frecuentemente considerado un clásico: "'Dream Baby Dream', 'Che', 'Ghost Rider'—estos perturbadores, toscos, hirvientes himnos de punk están entre los más visionarios y melódicos experimentos que el universo del rock ha producido hasta ahora."

Los álbumes de Suicide y sus presentaciones en vivo a finales de los 70s y principios de los 80s son considerados entre las grabaciones de que más influencia han tenido en el post punk y en darle forma al indie rock, industrial music y dance. Entre otros, Henry Rollins, Soft Cell, The Fleshtones y R.E.M. han mencionado a Suicide como una de sus principales influencias, y décadas más tarde Bruce Springsteen inesperadamente cantaría versiones de sus canciones en conciertos. Por otro lado, cancions de Springsteen como "Mr State Trooper" del álbum "Nebraska" son claramente influenciadas por Suicide.

Vega y Rev ambos han lanzado álbumes como solistas, y Suicide lanzó su primer álbum en más de una década en el 2002 con American Supreme. Las ventas, sin embargo, fueron lentas, y las críticas mixtas. . User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

info.wikipedia: Suicide Commando es una banda belga de música electro-industrial, creada por Johan Van Roy en 1986. Se encuentra fuertemente influenciada por bandas como Front 242, Skinny Puppy y Ministry. Con un sonido fuerte y agresivo es uno de los iconos de la música EBM. Su estilo es también conocido como electro dark y es considerada la banda fuente de este estilo.

own_scenes.desc: Anterior a la no wave y al punk, el arquetipo de la colisión neoyorquina entre arte y rock: Alan Vega, escultor de santuarios trash, y Martin Rev, músico de free jazz, nacidos del taller Project of Living Artists. Vega canta como un Elvis de ciencia ficción envuelto en ecos de Sun Records; Rev hace latidos con un teclado desvencijado y una caja de ritmos para bodas. Conciertos-agresión aprendidos de Iggy Pop. «Padrinos» literales de Lydia Lunch y James Chance.

refs.q: Suicide era, por muchos motivos, el arquetipo de esta colisión neoyorquina entre arce y rock
refs.para: Aunque anterior por varios años canco a la no wave como al punk, Suicide era, por muchos motivos, el arquetipo de esta colisión neoyorquina entre arce y rock. El cantante, Alan Vega, era un escultor que usaba lamparitas eléctricas y ready-mades (chucherías católicas kitsch, juguetes de plástico, naipes porno, fotos de celebridades) para crear santuarios trash a partir de su visión de una Norteamérica poscataclísmica del futuro cercano. A finales de la década del sesenta, se unió a la Art Workers' Coalition, un grupo socialista militante que, en una ocasión, levantó barricadas frente al Museo de Arte Moderno de Nueva York.

scenes.name: La blank generation (Akron, San Francisco, Manhattan)
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La «blank generation» nace de un vacío moral: la sociedad posindustrial reduce al individuo a un engranaje y la humanidad imagina su mutación en monstruos. La música de la new wave es una de las formas más filosóficas del rock. En Akron (Ohio), Pere Ubu (Modern Dance, «fresco de una civilización al borde del colapso» y folk para la era industrial), Devo, Styrenes, Waitresses, Dead Boys. En San Francisco, el tercer polo: los Residents (Meet The Residents, Not Available, Eskimo), Chrome (space-rock e implosiones industriales), Tuxedomoon, Factrix, Zoogz Rift, Rhythm And Noise, Negativland y Biota. En Manhattan, Suicide (sintetizador y voz; inventan el «psychobilly») y los Feelies.

podcast.title: "Punk Masses" Gigs
podcast.body: Inspired by Lester Bangs' December 1970 reference to Iggy Pop as a "stooge punk" in Cream Magazine, Alan Vega and his band Suicide began calling their gigs "punk masses," an early adoption of the term "punk" in a performance context. "He was in a band called Suicide, and they took that cream reference and started calling their gig punk masses."

podcast.body: Suicide is considered the absolute germ of the No Wave movement, particularly its musical aspect, possibly being the earliest pioneers in this sound. "de hecho yo creo que el german absoluto del movimiento no wave, es la banda suicide, suicide posiblemente fueron los primeros."

podcast.title: Anti-Commercial Philosophy
podcast.body: Suicide's philosophy was reactive against consumer music and large progressive rock concerts, which meant that achieving commercial success was not aligned with the No Wave movement's ethos. "Además, con esa filosofía totalmente reactiva que había en contra la música de consumo, la música del público, esos grandes concertos de rock progresivo, el que tuviesen exitos, lo mejor tampoco era muy corrente con un movimiento no wave."

podcast.title: Artists More Than Musicians
podcast.body: The members of Suicide were primarily artists, encompassing multiple disciplines such as photography, poetry, cinema collaboration, and art exhibitions, rather than solely musicians. "Y es que yo creo que eran más artistas que músicos. Los miembros de suicide apartaran fotógrafos eran poetas, colaboraron en el cine y hicieron exposiciones eran artistas, pues como un poco hay, de estos que dominaban muchas disciplinas y trabajaban en muchos distintos campos al mismo tiempo."

podcast.title: CBGB Scene Band
podcast.body: Suicide was one of the bands featured in the burgeoning CBGB scene, alongside Blondie, The Talking Heads, and The Heartbreakers, as the club became a central hub for new music. "CBGB was becoming the center of a new scene featuring bands with names like Blondie and Suicide and The Talking Heds and a television spin-off band called The Heartbreakers."

podcast.title: Early Performances at CBGB
podcast.body: Suicide was one of the significant bands playing at CBGB by the summer of 1974, contributing to the vibrant scene that established the club as a pivotal location for new and emerging forms of music, including punk. "By the summer of 1974, Hilly's bar, now known just as CBGB to everyone, was hosting not just television, but the Ramones, Patty Smith, Suicide, Blondie, Talking Heads, the Heartbreakers, and a bunch of other groups."

podcast.body: Suicide was one of the earliest two-piece bands remembered, performing around New York City in the early 1970s. xref.title: Nancy Spungen's Death (1978)
xref.body: On October 12, 1978, Sid Vicious awoke from a heroin haze to discover his girlfriend, Nancy Spungen, dead from stab wounds in the bathroom of their room at the Chelsea Hotel in New York, with his knife found in her stomach. xref.title: Death by Suicide (1980)
xref.body: Ian Curtis died by his own hand on May 18th, 1980, at the age of 23. His health had been very poor, exacerbated by epileptic seizures, a mix of prescriptions, drinking, illegal drug use, a poor diet, and late nights. He was also under immense pressure from an impending divorce, an affair, financial worries, and the demands of performing with his band, Joy Division. "Ian died by his own hand on May 18th, 1980."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death by Suicide (May 18, 1980)
xref.body: Ian Curtis died by suicide on May 18, 1980, at the age of 23. He had been in very poor health, suffering from epileptic seizures exacerbated by a "crazy cocktail" of prescriptions, drinking, illegal drug use, poor diet, and late nights. He also faced an impending divorce, an affair with a Belgian woman, money worries, and pressure to continue performing with Joy Division despite his problems. The final Joy Division show on May 2, 1980, saw Ian faint during the last song, experiencing another grand mal seizure, leading to the cancellation of their upcoming North American tour. On the evening of May 17, Ian returned to his home at 77 Barton Street in Macclesfield, Manchester. His wife Deborah was out. He watched the 1977 film "Strozek," drank strong coffee and whiskey, and then wrote a long note to Deborah all night. As the sun rose on May 18, he put on his favorite album, "The Idiot" by Iggy Pop, went to the garden for a length of rope from the clothesline, and hanged himself. Deborah found him a few hours later. "He'd been in very poor health, suffering from epileptic seizures that were exacerbated by a crazy cocktail of prescriptions, drinking illegal drug use, poor diet late nights, an impending divorce, and a ferry was having with a woman from Belgium worries about money and pressures to keep on performing with the band despite all these problems."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Near-Death Experience and Recovery (1995-1996)
xref.body: From late spring 1995 through to a brief clinical death in 1996, Dave Gahan's life was consumed by heroin addiction, costing $3,000 daily, leading to extreme dissociation, conversations with stuffed animals (including a Bugs Bunny doll), and two suicide attempts. On May 27, 1996, after an attempt to record with Martin Gore, Gahan injected cocaine and heroin at the Sunset Marquis Hotel in Hollywood, leading to full cardiac arrest and two minutes of clinical death. He recalled a vision of his wife screaming for him to return and a voice stating, "This is wrong, you don't get to decide." His recovery began after summer 1996, largely influenced by the threat of green card revocation from the American government if he didn't enter rehab and remain sober. He has been sober since June 6, 1996, now runs four times a week, lives in New York's West Village, and is married to Jennifer, his third wife. "He was for all intents and purposes clinically dead for two full minutes. He now says he remembers the vision of his wife screaming at him to come back to this plane."

xref.title: Death at Ritz Carlton Double Bay Hotel (November 22-23, 1997)
xref.body: Michael Hutchence's final hours began after dinner with his father and stepmother in Sydney on November 22, 1997, where he subsequently returned to room 524 at the Ritz Carlton Double Bay Hotel. He had champagne, daiquiris, and beer with his ex-girlfriend Kim Wilson and her current boyfriend in the hotel bar, continuing to his room for a nightcap. After they left at 4 AM, he made several unanswered phone calls to ex-girlfriends. Early on November 23rd, he mailed some letters, appearing "pretty rough" to the clerk. Housekeeping discovered him dead around noon, the room in disarray with prescription pills scattered and furniture moved. He died between 9:50 and 10:30 AM, having been strangled by a belt hung on a door. His cause of death has been debated, with official findings concluding auto-erotic asphyxiation, though suicide was also considered, despite no note. "Michael was dead. He had been strangled by a belt hung on a door."

xref.title: Mike Suzuki's Cold Case Review (April 2014)
xref.body: In April 2014, 20 years after Kurt Cobain's death, Seattle Police cold case detective Mike Suzuki reviewed the original file and released new photos. After a decade of experience with cold cases, Suzuki concluded that "The investigation on the death of Kurt Cobain, which was conducted 20 years ago, reached the correct conclusion of the manner of death was suicide." His review uncovered a sale slip for 20 gauge shotgun shells from Seattle Guns and information about a cab driver dropping someone, likely Kurt, near the store on April 2, 1994. He also used 35-millimeter film to reconstruct the gun firing, confirming "nothing weird" about the spent shell or gun's position, thereby dismantling theories of a staged suicide. "The investigation on the death of Kurt Cobain, which was conducted 20 years ago, reached the correct conclusion of the manner of death was suicide."

xref.title: Bataclan Terrorist Attack (November 13, 2015)

xref.title: Death (May 17–18, 2017) – MGM Grand Detroit, Ativan, Unknown Barbiturates, Naloxone Found in System
xref.body: After a Soundgarden show at the MGM Grand in Detroit, Cornell returned to room 1136. His wife Vicki, 2,000 miles away in Los Angeles, noticed the house lights flickering via a remote app on Chris's phone and called him at 11:35pm — twenty minutes after he left the stage. His bodyguard Martin had given him two Ativan (lorazepam) tablets beforehand to help him sleep. Cornell told Vicki he was fine but sounded groggy and slurred. Martin was sent to check on him at 12:15am, found the room locked, kicked the door in, found the bathroom locked, kicked that door in, and found Chris on the floor with blood from his mouth and an exercise band around his neck. A hotel medic arrived at 12:56am; paramedics followed; Chris was pronounced dead at 1:30am. The official cause was suicide by hanging. Toxicology found Ativan, unknown barbiturates, and unexplained Nalozone (naloxone, an anti-opioid) in his system. A hidden injury was mentioned in two clinical reports but not in the autopsy. In 2018 Vicki sued Dr. Robert Coblin of Beverly Hills, who had prescribed the Ativan, alleging dangerous over-prescription to a known former addict; the lawsuit settled out of court in May 2021. "Many of us who know Chris well noticed that he wasn't himself during his final hours and that something was very off."

Despite a vacation with his family in Arizona, Bennington returned to LA for an alleged Linkin Park video shoot, but "something went very wrong" that evening. No drugs or significant alcohol were found, and his autopsy revealed nothing of concern in his blood, leaving his motivations largely unknown. "The only possible clue is that July 20 would have been Chris Cornell's 53rd birthday."

xref.title: Death by Suicide (May 18, 2017)
xref.body: Chris Cornell died by suicide by hanging on May 18, 2017, at 1:30 AM, a death that came as a "real shock" to many. He was found in his hotel room (room 1136 at the MGM Grand, Detroit) with a red exercise band around his neck, attached to a carabiner jammed tightly into the doorframe. The night before, May 17, Soundgarden played a show at the Fox Theatre in Detroit, after which his long-time tour manager felt Chris was "messed up and struggling." Back at the hotel, his bodyguard, Martin Kirsten, gave him two Ativan pills, for which Chris had a prescription. Shortly after, Chris spoke to his wife Vicki, who noted his slurred speech; he claimed to have taken "too much Ativan" and was "just tired." He abruptly hung up, alarming Vicki. Martin Kirsten, called by Vicki, found Chris's room latched from the inside. After kicking open both the room and bathroom doors, he found Chris. The toxicology report found Ativan (four doses), pseudoephedrine, butylbital, caffeine, and Narcan (administered by paramedics). While his wife speculated drugs contributed to an "altered mental state," the police ruled it suicide by hanging. "Chris was pronounced dead at 1.30, and the police ruled a suicide by hanging."

xref.title: Death in Detroit (2017)
xref.body: Chris Cornell passed away on May 18, 2017, in room 1136 of the MGM Grand Hotel in Detroit. The tragedy occurred shortly after Soundgarden had performed at the nearby Fox Hotel. Feeling anxious after the show and fearing insomnia, Cornell took a couple of Ativan tablets. He spoke to his wife at 11:35 PM, then his bodyguard found him at 12:15 AM in a locked bathroom with a red exercise band around his neck and blood from his mouth after kicking in the door. He was declared dead at 1:30 AM, with the coroner ruling it suicide by hanging. His widow, Vicki Cornell, subsequently sued his doctor for prescribing Ativan. "At 130, Chris Cornell was declared dead. A coroner's report would rule that it was suicide, death by hanging."

xref.title: Discovery of Death (2017)
xref.body: Concerned by Chris's abrupt hang-up, Vicki called Martin Kirsten, who returned to room 1136 around 12:15 AM, approximately 40 minutes after his last departure. Despite having a key, the door was latched from the inside. Security refused to open it without authorization, so Kirsten kicked the door open. After searching the room and finding the bathroom door locked, he kicked that open as well. Inside, Cornell was found on the floor with blood around his mouth and a red exercise band around his neck, which was attached to a carabiner tightly jammed into the doorframe. Paramedics arrived just before 1 AM, but it was too late. Chris was pronounced dead at 1:30 AM, with police ruling it a suicide by hanging. "Inside, Cornell was found laying on the floor, blood running down his mouth and a red exercise band around his neck. The band had been attached to a carbonyl, which is a type of shackle."

It also has high rainfall (up to seven feet annually) and one of the highest suicide rates in the state. Historically, 60 years prior, it was a port for sailors with up to 50 brothels. "Now Aberdeen is this really dreary logging town. It's about an hour west of Olympia. The place features lots of trailer parks, many of which allegedly harbor grow-ops for pot and magic mushrooms. And there's lots of crystal meth. It's the way some people supplement their incomes now that the logging industries in trouble. There's a new biodiesel project, but you know, that can only do so much. Maybe they should go back to hosting Bordeaux. Sixty years ago Aberdeen was a place where sailors would put into port and at one point the place had up to 50 brothels that happily serviced them. And not only is Aberdeen in this perpetual economic decline, but it can also get up to seven feet. And yes, I did say seven feet of rain per year. So no wonder the place is one of the highest suicide rates in the state."

xref.title: Kurt Cobain's Death Controversy
xref.body: The short answer to whether Kurt Cobain was murdered is "no." However, many conspiracy theories persist, citing "unanswered questions" such as how he could inject a massive heroin overdose, put his gear away, and shoot himself before being incapacitated, the alleged change in handwriting on his suicide note, who used his credit card post-mortem, and why a room above the garden house wasn't checked during searches. These questions have fueled documentaries, books, and websites. Applying Occam's Razor, the "simplest answer is usually the correct one." Kurt was described as a depressed, unhealthy, hardcore heroin addict who associated with "very weird and bad people," had an obsession with guns, and was "certifiably suicidal." His body was so accustomed to heroin that a fatal dose might have had a delayed effect, allowing him time to put away a syringe and aim the gun. The murder theory is deemed "just chasing shadows," though the possibility of being wrong is acknowledged. "My short answer to this is no. Now there are all sorts of unanswered questions. How did Kurt manage to inject himself with a massive overdose of heroin, put his gear away in the maneuver the shot got in time before the drugs knocked him out? What about the fact that the handwriting on the suicide note appears to change? Who was using Kurt's credit card in the hours and days after he died? Why didn't anyone think to check the room above the garden house when they were searching for him?"

xref.title: Louisiana Proposed Law – Fines Up to $2,000 for Selling a Marilyn Manson CD to a Minor
xref.body: A proposed Louisiana law sought to prohibit the sale of "lyrics harmful to minors," defining "harmful" broadly to include topics such as rape, incest, and suicide. It would have imposed fines of up to $2,000 for selling a Marilyn Manson CD to a person under 17 who was unmarried. "Would have imposed fines of up to $2,000 for selling a Marilyn Manson CD to a minor under 17 who was not married."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Missed American Tour and Triumph
xref.body: Ian Curtis committed suicide just hours before Joy Division was scheduled to embark on their very first American tour. This tragic event occurred on the eve of what was perceived as a potential "gigantic, artistic, and commercial triumph" for the group. "Ian Curtis hung himself literally just hours before Joy Division was supposed to leave on their very first American tour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Multiple Overdoses and Suicide Attempt
xref.body: Dave Gahan experienced several overdoses during the Devotional Tour, including one incident between the main set and the encore that rendered him unconscious. His drug use escalated after the tour, leading to paranoia, conversations with stuffed animals, carrying a gun, and a suicide attempt in August 1995 where he slashed his wrists. "Dave managed to overdose a couple of times on the tour including one occasion where a bump between the main set and the encour knocked him cold. There was a suicide attempt in August 1995 when he slashed his wrists and there were plenty of overdoses."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Murder and Ritual Suicide
xref.body: John Nödtveidt, associated with the band Dissection, murdered a gay man from Algeria and subsequently served time in jail for the crime. After his release from prison, Nödtveidt committed ritual suicide. "John Notvelt was with a band called Dissection. He murdered a gay man from Algeria and was sent to jail. And when he got out, he committed ritual suicide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Murder in the Chelsea Hotel
xref.body: Nancy Spungin died in Room 100 of the Chelsea Hotel between 8 and 10 AM on October 12, 1978. She was found in the bathroom under the sink, having been stabbed in the lower abdomen with a Jaguar Wilderness K-11 knife, causing fatal external and internal hemorrhaging. The medical examiner concluded it was murder, not suicide. "It was 10.45 on the morning of Thursday, October 12th, 1978. Sid was in shock, initially in a panic. He confessed, I stabbed her, but I never meant to kill her."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Sid Vicious and Questions About the Murder of Nancy Spungen

xref.title: Official Cause of Death and Alternative Theories
xref.body: His death on November 22, 1997, was officially ruled a suicide. However, in 1999, Paula Yates suggested on *60 Minutes* Australia that he died from auto-erotic asphyxiation gone wrong, a theory the coroner explicitly rejected due to lack of forensic evidence. This theory gained widespread belief, fueled by Hutchence's known sexual kinks, his mother's mention of him being with sadomasochists, and his own comments about seeking the "ultimate sexual high." "Again, the corner rule that Michael Hutchins died by his own hand in that hotel room on November 22, 1997. But then in 1999, Paula Yates made a suggestion. Totally contrary to everything she'd said up until that point. On the Australian version of 60 minutes, she intimated that Michael may have died as the result of solo sex play gone wrong. Auto-erotic asphyxiation, which he took too far."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: On-Stage Collapse and Overdose Attempt
xref.body: On April 4, 1980, during a show with The Stranglers at London's Rainbow venue, Ian suffered three epileptic attacks within the first five songs before completely collapsing; the band struggled to intervene earlier due to the difficulty of distinguishing his seizures from his characteristic dancing. Three days later, on April 7, Ian deliberately overdosed on his epilepsy medication, leaving a suicide note, and required a stomach pump at the hospital, yet a psychiatrist controversially declared him "not suicidal." "Three days later, Ian purposely overdosed on his epilepsy medication."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Path to Punk Rock
xref.body: Two significant factors led Joe Strummer to become a punk rocker: his discovery of rock music around age 10, and the suicide of his brother, David. Following these events, Joe actively turned his back on his upper-middle-class upbringing and immersed himself in the punk rock lifestyle. "The things that put Joe in the road to being a punk were A, his discovery of rock music at about age 10, and B, his brother David's suicide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Performance Spill-Over and Police Intervention
xref.body: His chaotic performances often extended into the streets, and police presence was a regular occurrence at his shows due to their extreme nature. "Sometimes his performances would spill out onto the street. And always, always, always. He was threatening suicide. Sometimes he promised that he would take people with him. So no wonder cops were a regular thing at his shows."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Personal Adversities and Neurological Conditions
xref.body: Florence Welch's background includes emotional challenges such as her parents' divorce and the deaths of three grandparents; one died slowly, another, an art historian, committed suicide, and a third, who had encouraged her musical pursuits, died of a stroke. Florence also lives with dyslexia and dyspraxia, a neurological disorder impacting coordination and sometimes short-term memory, which she manages with therapies and which influences her art. "Florence is dyslexic and has something called dyspraxia, which is a neurological disorder that affects the messages the brain gives to other parts of the body when it comes to coordinating movements."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Personal Impact of Terry's Mental Health
xref.body: The "Ziggy" experience was incredibly intense for all involved, and Bowie was also deeply affected by his adored half-brother, Terry, who suffered terribly from manic depression and schizophrenia and required hospitalization. Terry later died by suicide more than a decade later, by lying down in front of a train. "Not only had the Ziggy experience been crazy for all involved, but he also had a half brother. He adored named Terry, who was suffering terribly with mental health issues."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Personal Struggles and Fragile Nature
xref.body: Chester Bennington battled significant personal issues throughout his life, including childhood abuse, addiction to cocaine and methamphetamine, a drinking problem, persistent depression, multiple failed attempts at rehabilitation, and previous suicide attempts. He was described as having a "certain fragile nature," finding solace in his friendship with Chris Cornell, with whom he often shared his struggles. "He had all sorts of issues, abused as a child, addiction to coke and meth, a drinking problem, lingering depression, failed attempts at rehab, a couple of suicide attempts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Personal Trauma and Health Conditions
xref.body: Florence Welch's background includes several emotional challenges: her parents divorced, a grandparent died slowly and painfully, another grandmother (an art historian) committed suicide, and her other grandmother (who encouraged her music) died of a stroke. Additionally, Florence is dyslexic and has dyspraxia, a neurological disorder affecting movement coordination, short-term memory, and directionality. "But then there's the emotional sign of her background. Her parents divorced. The slow, painful death of a grandparent."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Personal Turmoil and Suicide Attempt
xref.body: Ian Curtis faced significant personal challenges, including a difficult relationship with his wife Deborah, who had initiated divorce proceedings, and an affair with a Belgian fan, Enneke van Array. On April 6, 1980, he made a suicide attempt by overdosing on pills, requiring an ambulance and a stomach pump, yet a doctor inexplicably deemed him not suicidal and sent him home, after which he was so shaky at a gig that he could only perform two songs. "There was a suicide attempt on Sunday, April 6, 1980 when Ian died a bunch of pills." "He told his mates that he had a terrible claustrophobic feeling like he was caught in a whirlpool of being sucked down and drowning."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Plagiarism Claim Against Nirvana
xref.body: Killing Joke's song "80s" (1985), co-written by Jazz Coleman, was observed to have a guitar riff strikingly similar to Nirvana's "Come As You Are" (1991). The situation regarding a lawsuit remains unclear, with conflicting reports on whether action was taken or dropped after Kurt Cobain's death, or simply considered but not pursued for financial/personal reasons. "Some sources say that there was a lawsuit, but that it was dropped after Kurt Cobain commuted suicide. Others say that even though they considered suing, killing joke decided not to take any action on copyright infringement for personal and financial reasons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Music Retirement and Suicide Attempts
xref.body: After The Plasmatics broke up, Wendy O'Williams pursued acting and recorded some soul material before retiring. She subsequently made a series of suicide attempts, including one where she tried to stab herself in the heart but the knife got stuck in her sternum. "Then came a series of suicide attempts. Including the time she tried to jam a knife right into her own heart, but it became stuck in her sternum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-SNL Career Impact
xref.body: After the *Saturday Night Live* incident, Sinéad O'Connor's career became "pretty rocky." Despite releasing "very interesting and very good music," her outspokenness, rocky personal life, a suicide attempt, and bipolar disorder diagnosis prevented her from reaching her full career potential. "Since then, her career has been pretty rocky."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Postcard to Dave Grohl
xref.body: Seven Year Bitch sent a postcard to Dave Grohl following Kurt Cobain's suicide, understanding the grief he was experiencing. The message on the postcard encouraged him to continue with music: "We know what you're going through. The desire to play music is gone for now, but it will return. Don't worry." This message was a "deciding factor" in convincing Dave to keep making music. "It read, We know what you're going through. The desire to play music is gone for now, but it will return. Don't worry."

xref.title: Preceding School Suicides in the Area
xref.body: The tragic events of Jeremy Dell's suicide were not isolated in the Richardson area. In the years leading up to January 8, 1991, three other students in Richardson had taken their own lives. Furthermore, in 1985, a 17-year-old student had killed himself in front of his fellow drama students in nearby Arlington, highlighting a troubling pattern. "It could be because in the years previous to January 8, 1991, three students in Richardson had taken their own lives."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rebirth from Joy Division
xref.body: Following the suicide of singer Ian Curtis in May 1980, Joy Division was reborn as New Order, with Rob Gretton continuing as their manager. Gretton's involvement went beyond typical management, as he assisted the band with tasks like sorting song titles and even sang backup on some of their recordings.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reflections on Addiction and Sobriety (Ongoing)
xref.body: Dave Gahan reflected on his period of addiction as a "negative way of a permanent solution to a temporary problem," akin to living a constant suicide. He acknowledged the fear of change and the comfort found in misery, and the struggle to regain a sense of normalcy and happiness without drugs. He credited working with a vocal coach for providing confidence, self-worth, and daily structure in his recovery. "Trying to destroy myself is a really negative way of a permanent solution to a temporary problem."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Resilience in Attawapiskat
xref.body: Despite Attawapiskat being in the news for serious issues like housing crises, a major suicide epidemic, and drug problems, Adrian Sutherland and others like him refuse to give up on their home and neighbors, highlighting a spirit of resilience. "From Anna Wapisgad in Northern Ontario, a place that's been in the news for so many sad reasons like housing crisis, a major suicide epidemic, drug problems and more. But guys like Adrian Sutherland refused to give up on their home and their neighbors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide
xref.body: Ian Curtis, the singer for Joy Division, committed suicide by hanging himself in his kitchen. "When Joy Division singer Ian Curtis committed suicide by hanging himself in his kitchen, he was married with a wife and daughter."

xref.title: Suicide (Two Years After Release)
xref.body: Two years after his release from prison, Nödtveidt died by suicide. His body was discovered arranged in a ring of candles, with a book of satanic rituals found beside him. "Two years later, Nonvite was dead by his own hand."

xref.title: Suicide Attempts After Bail – Slashing and Jumping
xref.body: After his release, Sid made two suicide attempts: first by slashing himself with a broken light bulb, and then by trying to jump out of a window at the Seville Hotel in New York. Both attempts were unsuccessful. "Sid attempts suicide by slashing himself with a broken light bulb. He messed that up so he tried to jump out of a window at the Seville Hotel in New York."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide Note Attempt and Mental Health
xref.body: On a night in September 2017, Dolores O'Riordan took sedatives, drank heavily, and began writing a suicide note, though she ultimately abandoned it. Her psychotherapist, assigned to her, reportedly did not express concern that she might attempt a similar act again. "And on a night in September 2017, she took some sedatives and started drinking heavily and began to write a suicide note."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide Note Excerpt
xref.body: The suicide note included a significant passage expressing his inability to fake enthusiasm for beautiful people and the music industry, stating he couldn't "take up with beautiful people off by thinking and pretending as if I'm having a hundred percent flood." It also contained the line "It's better to burn out than to fade away." "It's better to burn out than to fade away. Peace, love, empathy, Kurt Cobain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide Note and Death Pact Theory
xref.body: The purity of the heroin he consumed was known to Sid, having been informed by his mother. A note later found in his passport supported the theory of suicide, stating a "death pact" with Nancy and requesting burial next to her in his leather jacket, jeans, and motorcycle boots.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide Pact and Band Dissolution
xref.body: A solemn suicide pact existed among the members of Joy Division, stipulating that if any member were to leave the band for any reason, Joy Division would cease to exist. Consequently, upon Ian Curtis's death, Peter Hook, Barney Sumner, and Stephen Morris honored their word, retiring Joy Division and beginning work on their next project, New Order. "The deal was that should any member leave for any reason joy division would be broken up. So once Ian was gone, Peter Hook, Barney Sumner, and Stephen Morris kept their word."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide Runs in Kurt Cobain's Family Across Multiple Generations
xref.body: Kurt's great-great-grandfather John Cobain was a county sheriff who accidentally shot himself in 1938. His great-grandfather James Irving stabbed himself in the stomach in front of his family in 1935, was institutionalized, and died two months later after ripping out his own stitches. His great-uncle Burl Cobain shot himself in the stomach with a .38 in 1979; when that failed he shot himself in the head. At age 14, Kurt told friends he planned to kill himself one day after becoming a rock star. At 15 he and his stepbrother James made a short film called *Kurt Commits Bloody Suicide*. At 13 he wrote in his journals of planning to actually kill himself. At 16, drunk and stoned, he lay on train tracks with a large piece of cement on his chest waiting to be hit; the train went past on a different track. The famous March 1994 Rome hotel overdose was the last major attempt before his death on April 5, 1994 (aged 27) in his Seattle home. "He said he had suicide genes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide and Band's Re-formation
xref.body: Ian Curtis was the singer of Joy Division. His suicide in 1980 led directly to the remaining members of the band forming New Order. "When singer Ian Curtis committed suicide in 1980, the rest of the band regrouped as new order."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide and Final Moments
xref.body: Julee Cruise died by suicide on June 9th at the age of 65, with her husband playing "Rome," her favorite B-52's song, during her final moments. "Her end came on June 9th at the age of 65. She took her own life with her husband playing Rome, her favorite B-52 song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide and Legacy
xref.body: Jim Ellison, the singer for Material Issue, tragically committed suicide, which derailed the band's career. His life and music left a lasting impact, inspiring The Tragically Hip's song "Escape is at Hand for the Traveling Man" and being honored by the annual "International Pop Over Throw" festival in Chicago. "However, their spirit lives on. Chicago, host an annual festival called International Pop Over Throw that's been going on since 1997, and it features bands in the whole PowerPop vein."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide by Hanging
xref.body: After a tumultuous period marked by a collapsing marriage, his mistress's demands, and severe anxiety about the upcoming North American tour, Ian spent the night of May 17, 1980, alone at 77 Barton Street. He watched the 1977 film "Strozek," drank strong coffee and whiskey, wrote a long note to Deborah with pictures of his wife and baby daughter nearby, then put on Iggy Pop's "The Idiot," and, as the sun rose on Sunday, May 18th, he took a length of rope from the clothesline and hanged himself at the age of 23, discovered by Deborah hours later. "Then he went out into the garden and got himself a length of rope from the clothesline. And as the sun came up and he sang, Ian hanged himself."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide's Impact on Goth Scene
xref.body: Ian Curtis's suicide contributed to the dark atmosphere and themes prevalent in the developing Goth scene. "And then Ian Curtis of Joy Division committed suicide at adding fuel to that fire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suspicion of Murder Despite Suicide Note
xref.body: Despite a suicide note and a history of ADHD, depression, suicidal ideation, drug use, and heavy drinking, police, the coroner, and fans remained suspicious of Elliot Smith's death. The primary reason for this suspicion was the absence of "hesitation wounds," as he had stabbed himself cleanly twice directly in the heart. "Police were still suspicious. The corner was suspicious and fans remain suspicious. Why? Mainly because there were no hesitation wounds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Television Spin-off and CBGB Scene Involvement
xref.body: The Heartbreakers were identified as a "television spin-off band" and were part of the burgeoning CBGB scene, alongside Blondie, Suicide, and The Talking Heads, as the club became a central hub for new music. "CBGB was becoming the center of a new scene featuring bands with names like Blondie and Suicide and The Talking Heds and a television spin-off band called The Heartbreakers."

xref.title: The Stolen Gun and Suicide Notes
xref.body: Around Christmas, Jeremy Dell falsely claimed he received a gun as a present, but it appears he stole a .357 Magnum from a drawer at his dad's girlfriend's house. In early January 1991, he started writing and sending suicide notes to friends, some thoughts even recorded on cassette. One letter ominously read, "This letter was written before I committed suicide," concluding with a postscript: "PS. Call my dad for funeral info." "Sometime around Christmas, Jeremy mentioned that he was given a gun as a present. This is not true. It appears that he stole it from a drawer at the house of dad's girlfriend."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tragic Accidental Drowning
xref.body: On the evening of May 29, 1997, while in Memphis to record new material, Jeff Buckley went for a swim in Wolf River Harbor, which connects to the Mississippi River. He had swum there before, but this time he entered the water fully clothed and wearing heavy boots. While floating on his back and singing the chorus to Led Zeppelin's "Whole Lotta Love," a boat passed by, creating a wake that caused him to disappear. His body was found five days later downstream. The death was ruled an accidental drowning, with no drugs or alcohol involved and no indication of suicide. He was 30 years old. "Everything was going absolutely according to plan until the evening of May 29, 1997. Jeff was in Memphis to record some new material, and that night he and Keith Fulti, a rodean is banned, sat on the bank of Wolf River Harbor, which is connected to the Mississippi River, listening to music. Jeff had gone swimming there a few times before, and decided to do it again. So he went into the water. This time he was fully clothed and wearing big, heavy boots. He floated out on his back and began seeing the chorus to Led Zeppelin's whole lot of love. But then a boat came by, stirring up a big wake, and with that, Jeff was gone. His body was found five days later down River. No drugs, no alcohol, nothing to indicate suicide. It was a straight, accidental drowning. He was 30 years old."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tragic Death
xref.body: A few months after giving a radio interview in early 2017 where he openly discussed his mental health battles, Chester Bennington died by suicide. "A few months after that interview, Chester would be gone, taking his own life."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tragic End of Singer
xref.body: Material Issue's career was "derailed by the sudden suicide of singer Jim Ellison." Despite this tragedy, their spirit continues, notably through an annual Powerpop festival in Chicago named "International Pop Over Throw," inspired by their album title. "I love these guys, but they were derailed by the sudden suicide of singer Jim Ellison."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tragic Suicide
xref.body: Mark Linkous's battle with depression persisted despite his continued musical work. While in the process of divorcing his wife of 19 years, he took his own life in Knoxville, Tennessee. He used a rifle, aiming it at his heart, and at the time of his death, he had a blood alcohol level of .43, with various antidepressants and anti-anxiety medications found in his system. "Then, while on the process of a divorce from his wife of 19 years, he took a rifle, went for a walk, sat down on an alley in Knoxville, Tennessee, aimed the gun at his heart and pulled the trigger."

xref.body: GG Allin was buried in his leather jacket and jockstrap, with the mortician specifically instructed not to wash or clean the body. At his funeral, friends filled his mouth with whiskey and drugs, and he was buried wearing headphones playing his 1989 album, `The Suicide Sessions`. "GG was buried in his leather jacket and juxtap. The more Titian was ordered not to wash anything or otherwise clean up the body. At his funeral, friends filled his mouth with whiskey and drugs."

xref.title: Unresolved Case and Theories
xref.body: The coroner could not definitively determine whether Bobby Fuller's death was a suicide, an accident, or a murder, leading to an unsolved case that has spurred TV shows and books. Theories include a postulation by his bandmate Jim Reese linking Charles Manson (though Manson was in prison) and a theory suggesting the LAPD staged his death due to Fuller's connection to a woman tied to the mob. "The corner couldn't say for sure. There are theories though. Jim Reese, who played in Bobby's band, postulated that Charles Manson had something to do with it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Unusual Nature of Stab Wounds
xref.body: The method of Elliot Smith's death, two clean stabs directly to the heart without hesitation, is highly unusual for suicide. Statistics indicate that only 4% of suicides involve sharp force trauma, predominantly wrist-slashing. The act of turning a knife sideways and plunging it between the ribs twice without hesitation is considered an extremely painful way to die, fueling theories among fans that "bad drug buddies" might have been involved. "According to statistics on suicide, only 4% of people take their own lives with sharp force trauma and almost all of those involve wrist-slashing."
